LESSON: VOLUME

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: VOLUME
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers VOLUME, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can you work out the volume of cubes and cuboids?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. Sign terms related to volume,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of VOLUME in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. pile objects into stacks of cubes and cuboids in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of VOLUME in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. Work out volume of cuboids by piling blocks to form a cuboid,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of VOLUME in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. calculate the volume of cubes by piling blocks to form a cube,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of VOLUME in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. use digital devices other resources for learning about volume,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of VOLUME in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on VOLUME together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: learners practise stacking objects or blocks to form cubes and cuboids of different sizes.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: as learners count the number of objects in the pile that makes a cube to

determine the volume.

Values:
• Unity: learners discuss and carefully arrange blocks or objects on top of each other into cuboid and cube shape.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: learners safely play games involving stacking blocks to form cubes and cuboids.

Link to other learning areas

The learner is able to relate arranging blocks or objects on top of each other into cuboid and cube shapes to the Construction of food

preservation equipment in Agriculture and Nutrition.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Cubes, cuboids, print texts, relevant digital devices
